stem: What does 'void' mean in a method signature?
explanation: void = no return value - what GCSE called a procedure. A method with a return type is what GCSE called a function.
Value types are passed as a COPY - the method doubled its own copy and threw it away. To affect the caller use ref, or return the new value.
The parameter copies the REFERENCE, so both point at the same array - changes to its contents are visible to the caller. (Reassigning the parameter itself would not be.)

stem: What must a method do with an out parameter?
options: Assign it on every path before returning
explanation: out means 'I will definitely give you a value' - the compiler enforces assignment on every path. This is the TryParse pattern.

stem: Which pair is a VALID overload?
options: int F(int x) and string F(int x)
int F(int x) and int F(int x, int y)
int F(int x) and int F(int y)
explanation: Overloads must differ in their PARAMETER LIST. Return type alone (option A) or parameter name alone (option C) is not enough.

stem: Given Greet(string name, string greeting = "Hello"), what does Greet("Ada") produce?
options: Greeting Ada with an empty greeting
explanation: An omitted optional parameter takes its default - greeting becomes "Hello". Named arguments let you skip middle parameters: Greet("Ada", punctuation: "?").

stem: static int Total(params int[] xs)  - which call is INVALID?
explanation: params accepts no arguments, a comma-separated list, or a real array - all three work. It must be the last parameter.

stem: What happens if a recursive method has no base case?
explanation: Every call adds a stack frame; without a base case the stack fills and the process dies with StackOverflowException - one of the few exceptions you cannot catch.

stem: What is  static double Square(double x) => x * x;  shorthand for?
options: A full method with { return x * x; }
explanation: The => here is an expression-bodied METHOD - identical to the braced version, just shorter. (The same arrow means something different in lambdas.)
ref passes the variables themselves, so the tuple swap really exchanges the caller's x and y - printing 2 1. Note ref is required at the call site too.
